skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting

skills.name: user-app-development

1. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
2. use vstd::arithmetic::power2::pow2;
3. 
4. verus! {
5. 
6. // =================================================================================================
7. // Abstract models of frame-number quantities, realized by the verified `arch` crate.
8. //
9. // `FrameNumber` is a newtype defined in the `arch` crate. Its real `#[verus_spec]` contracts (a
10. // `View` giving the integer index `frame@`, and the associated bound `FrameNumber::spec_max()`)
11. // supersede the former placeholder `assume_specification`s. These helpers re-expose those arch
12. // quantities under the names the kernel proofs already use.
13. // =================================================================================================
14. 
15. // The integer index (raw value) of a frame number: its `arch` view.
16. pub open spec fn spec_frame_raw_value(frame: FrameNumber) -> int {
17.     frame@
18. }
19. 
20. // The largest representable frame index (the `arch` bound `FrameNumber::spec_max()`).
21. pub open spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int {
22.     FrameNumber::spec_max() as int
23. }
24. 
25. // =================================================================================================
26. // Derived spec helpers over the `PhysicalAddress` view (its `int` raw address).
27. // =================================================================================================
28. 
29. // The frame an address belongs to: `addr / FRAME_SIZE` (equivalently `addr >> FRAME_SHIFT`).
30. pub open spec fn spec_frame_number(addr_view: int) -> int {
31.     addr_view / spec_page_size()
32. }
33. 
34. // The base address of a frame: `frame_index * FRAME_SIZE`.
35. pub open spec fn spec_from_number(frame_view: int) -> int {
36.     frame_view * spec_page_size()
37. }
38. 
39. impl PhysicalAddress {
40.     // Well-formedness: the address has a representable frame number. This is exactly what makes
41.     // `into_frame_number` total (its internal `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never
42.     // panics). `open` so callers' proofs (frame allocator, page tables) can rely on totality.
43.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
44.         spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
45.     }
46. }
47. 
48. // =================================================================================================
49. // Dependency contracts for not-yet-verified modules.
50. //
51. // `VirtualAddress` (the `sys` crate) and `FRAME_SHIFT` (the `arch` crate) are not yet
52. // verified. They are given trusted external specifications so that the verified `PhysicalAddress`
53. // bodies can be translated. These declarations are placeholders: when the underlying modules are
54. // verified, their real specifications will supersede these.
55. // =================================================================================================
56. 
57. // Note: `VirtualAddress::new` now carries its own verified `#[verus_spec]` in the `sys` crate
58. // (`result@ == value as int`), so its placeholder `assume_specification` was removed — the real
59. // specification supersedes it.
60. 
61. // Trusted contract for `VirtualAddress::into_raw_value`. Unlike `new`, this method CANNOT be
62. // verified in the `sys` crate due to a genuine Verus limitation: it is a trait-impl method
63. // (`<VirtualAddress as Address>::into_raw_value`), and Verus requires an *entire* trait impl to be
64. // verified as a unit ("In order to verify any items of this trait impl, the entire impl must be
65. // verified"). The same `impl Address for VirtualAddress` block contains `as_ptr` / `as_mut_ptr`,
66. // whose `usize as *const u8` / `usize as *mut u8` int-to-pointer casts Verus does not support
67. // ("Verus does not support this cast: `usize` to `*const u8`"). Annotating the block therefore
68. // breaks `make verify-sys` (empirically confirmed: commit history shows the annotation regressed
69. // sys from PASS to a compilation/setup error). Verifying it would instead require `external_body`
70. // on `as_ptr` / `as_mut_ptr`, which would *expand* the trusted base rather than shrink it. This
71. // single placeholder is therefore retained and documented under "External crate (`sys`)" in
72. // `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`; its body (`self.0`) trivially satisfies `result as int == self@`.
73. // Isolated reproducers: `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-hal-phys-address/specification/`.
74. pub assume_specification[ <::sys::mm::VirtualAddress as ::sys::mm::Address>::into_raw_value ](
75.     addr: VirtualAddress,
76. ) -> (result: usize)
77.     ensures
78.         result as int == addr@,
79. ;
80. 
81. // Note: `arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT` now carries its own verified modeling in the `arch` crate
82. // (`#[verus_verify]` on the constant, transparently `PAGE_SHIFT`), so its placeholder
83. // `assume_specification` was removed — the real definition supersedes it. The facts the proofs
84. // relied on (`FRAME_SHIFT < 32` and `spec_page_size() == pow2(FRAME_SHIFT)`) now follow from the
85. // transparent constant values together with `vstd`'s `lemma2_to64` (see `into_frame_number`).
86. 
87. // Note: `FrameNumber::from_raw_value` / `into_raw_value` now carry their own verified `#[verus_spec]`
88. // contracts in the `arch` crate, so their placeholder `assume_specification`s were removed — the
89. // real specifications supersede them (see `spec_frame_raw_value` / `spec_max_frame_number` above,
90. // which now re-expose the arch quantities).
91. 
92. } // verus!
